analysis.title: GS Contessa - US EQUITIES COLOR CHOPPY 8 Oct 2026
key_insights: S&P 500 closed -47bps at 7,765 with a $4.2Bn market-on-close imbalance to buy. NDX -139bps at 30,725, R2K +8bps at 2,795, Dow +10bps at 51,231. Volume was 18.827bn shares vs a YTD daily average of 18.628bn.

Trading was choppy and top-down, with ETF share of the tape near 32%, the highest since June. Focus was on headlines that Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the midterms, and that OpenAI annualised revenue is $20B less than previously signalled.
The GS desk saw long-only and hedge fund supply in large-cap tech after the OpenAI revenue headline.

Other drivers of semis/AI weakness: underwhelming Samsung and TSM prints against high expectations, reports that major AI players (ORCL, AVGO, SCPX) plan to tap debt markets further, and no update on the China optical ban weighing on US optical names (COHR, LITE, GLW).
About 70% of S&P constituents finished up, with RTY > SPX > NDX. RTY held its 200-day moving average as yields fell in the afternoon, ending a 4-day streak of underperformance vs SPX.
GS floor activity was a 4 on a 1-10 scale. Flows were -686bps better for sale, driven by overlapping supply in macro expressions and large-cap tech.

Consumer: CMG +8% and SBUX -160bps on headlines that Starbucks has explored a takeover of Chipotle, which would be the largest restaurant-sector deal ever. SBUX CEO Brian Niccol was formerly CEO of CMG.

Healthcare: XLV gave back its prior-day outperformance on a defensive bid and risk-off, with no single cause identified. One-offs cited: ARGX -12%, a reversal in Tools after AI drug discovery euphoria earlier in the week, and managed care jitters before imminent Medicare STARs ratings. HUM +12% post-bell on Medicare STARs results.
T, VZ and TMUS each traded about -3% after hours on a report that SpaceX is to buy a nationwide low-band spectrum license portfolio.

Derivatives: fixed-strike vols fell before the OpenAI headline while skew held a bid. Skew became more bid into the afternoon, and fixed-strike vols closed little changed in SPX and RUT. NDX vol underperformed along with spot, since positioning remains concentrated in the AI trade, and NDX vol has not performed as the index moved away from all-time highs.
Flow: a customer bought 10k SPX 31Dec 7300 puts at an average of 76.60. Single-stock and thematic flow was defensive, with downside trades in cyclical names alongside index-level hedges.

Clients traded options on GS's SPX ex-AI basket (SPXXAI) as a cleaner way to isolate the AI trade. The GS hybrids desk traded a SPXXAI higher / rates lower structure and considers it interesting given the backdrop.
The S&P implied move through the end of the week is 0.47%. The GS baskets team flagged that the divergence between the S&P 500 and the S&P ex-AI is now nearly 10% over about 5 weeks.
